text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN

- The economic coordination committee of the caretaker cabinet has decided to withdraw the subsidy on sugar and has directed the Ministry of Industries and the state-run Utility Stores Corporation to sell sugar at market rates.

- Deposed prime minister Benazir Bhutto said her party was following a twin strategy of mass mobilisation and legal battle as there was no consensus in her party on whether or not to boycott the elections.
- The Lahore High Court rejected a plea for referendum on "accountability before polls" saying the constitution cannot be amended through a popular vote.

- Sindh province caretaker Chief Minister Mumtaz Ali Bhutto held meetings with the president, the caretaker prime minister and the army chief and discussed a proposed relief package for the jailed activists of the Mohajir National Movement (MQM).
- China will complete the installation of the Chashma Nuclear Power Plant in Pakistan this year, the head of the China National Nuclear Corporation said in Beijing.
- The Indian Defence Ministry said a pilotless Pakistani aircraft which intruded into Indian air-space was fired upon. Pakistan has denied the claim.
- The Planning Commission's Deputy Chairman Hafeez Pasha said the caretaker government has been unable to completely overhaul the economic system.
- The first meeting of the tax reform commission on Sunday is expected to discuss levying general sales tax at the retail level and suggest a strategy for phasing out all tax exemptions.
BUSINESS RECORDER

- The European Commission has extended the deadline for a ban on seafood imports from Pakistan to July 1 to give the government time to complete formalities that would make the country eligible for exporting seafood.
- The Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission Hafeez Pasha said the liquid forex reserves would cross the $1 billion mark by the end of January.
- The government has asked a private gold importer to arrange a loan of $50 million, sources said.
THE NEWS
- Pakistani exporters have started exporting superior quality basmati rice to the European Union under new laws which ensure better quality.
- Pakistan has banned the import of animal bones from Afghanistan after foreign press reports suggesting that human bones were being mixed with animal bones.
THE MUSLIM
- The newly-formed Council for Defence and National Security is likely to strike down plans to buy 32 French-built Mirage 2000-5 military jets from France at a cost of $4 billion.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
